Celebrate 20 years since their inception, the ground-breaking, Grammy Award-winning ensemble The Infamous Stringdusters—whose tone and swagger meld acoustic majesty with the energy of a full-blown rock show—mark this milestone with the release of 20/20. Twenty brand new songs, born from endless miles in pursuit of a dream. Formed in Nashville in the early 2000s while performing as side-men with stalwarts of the bluegrass community, the band members soaked up every influence like musical sponges. Their friendships, paired with a shared drive to create their own music and master their own destiny, inevitably led to the birth of The Infamous Stringdusters. Alongside Chris Pandolfi (banjo), Travis Book (double bass), Jeremy Garrett (fiddle), Andy Hall (dobro), and Andy Falco (guitar), the group continues to fearlessly blur the boundaries between bluegrass, Americana, country, and indie-folk.

item.title: John Rock Loop Hike — Sat Oct 10, 9:00 AM
item.description:
WNC Sierra Club Join the WNC Sierra Club for a beautiful hike in the Pisgah National Forest. The John Rock Loop hike features around 1,100 feet of elevation gain up to a scenic overlook where we will have a snack and rest. This hike is about 5.9 miles in length and will take us approximately 3-4 hours. Be prepared for elevation gain and creek crossings. Make sure to pack food and water to stay nourished and hydrated! Wear gear that you are comfortable hiking in and good shoes. It is also a good idea to have rain gear just to be safe. If you are feeling unwell and/or have a fever, please help us to keep everyone safe and healthy by waiting for the next outing. Families, friends, and pets are all welcome. An adult must accompany all children. All dogs must remain on a leash and be friendly to all.
Please register using this [Link to John Rock Loop Hike Registration.](https://act.sierraclub.org/events/details?formcampaignid=701Po00002DA0ZMIA1)
YOU NEED TO EMAIL THE HIKE LEADER TO CONFIR

item.description:
Awakening Asheville Hosted by Tish Sjoberg
2nd and 4th Sundays
Now On-Line during Covid-19 Quarantine 10:00 a.m. – 12:15 p.m. $0 - $25 (Included in our monthly pass)
Slow down and be with yourself through art making. A rich morning that feeds your spirit, rests your body, quiets your mind and helps you remember who you are!
Here we will use the arts to have a conversation with ourselves and connect to our longings and gifts. This is not about religion, yet in the inquiry you may choose to make connections to your religious beliefs.
The format: We check in as a group, we may do a little drumming, have 5 minutes of quiet/reflection/meditation/prayer/relaxation time, go create art in silence (without talking) doing our own thing and then come back together to honor what we spent our time doing.

item.title: New Moon Circle for All with Marian Noble — Sun Oct 11, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville Join us for a welcoming and inclusive New Moon Circle, where all bodies and all genders are invited into sacred gathering. The New Moon is the seed point of the lunar cycle, a powerful time to pause, reflect, and plant clear intentions for the month ahead.
Our 90-minute circle opens with a grounding meditation to help you arrive fully in body and breath. We'll explore the astrological themes of this New Moon in an accessible way, then move into heart shares, holding space for one another in a supportive, non-judgmental circle. We'll close with a ritual aligned with this month's lunar energy to anchor your intentions.
You'll leave with greater clarity, deeper connection, and inspired momentum for the new lunar cycle. Whether you're new to moon rituals or a longtime practitioner, this circle offers insight, community, and renewal.

item.description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community.
